title: Route every list/table view through UnifiedTable to inherit the cold-load contract
statement: Do not hand-roll a table (rows, loading skeleton, empty state, entrance animation). Use the shared UnifiedTable and pass `columns` + `data` + `isLoading`; it renders a permanent column header, a geometry-matched delayed ghost while loading-into-empty, a settled-only empty state, and an id-guarded row-entrance cascade that is COUPLED to `isLoading` — so the whole loading-pattern-v2 doctrine comes from two props with no per-page skeleton.

title: Keep per-concept accent hues in one registry of literal class strings
statement: A concept's accent hue must live in ONE registry of full literal Tailwind class strings (never interpolated, so the scanner sees them); scattered local colorMaps let the same concept drift across three shades on three surfaces.

title: Make selection affordances real controls with non-colour status cues
statement: Selection affordances must be real controls (button with role=checkbox, aria-checked, aria-label=name — not a bare div); mixed selection sets el.indeterminate via a ref callback; status is never colour-alone (shape cue per WCAG 1.4.1); icon toggles carry aria-pressed; announcements use role=status aria-live=polite + sr-only.

title: Never import the English catalog at module scope to build user-visible labels
statement: `import { en }` at module scope freezes strings to English while LOOKING internationalized. Store a labelKey and resolve it at render time via useTranslation.

title: Adopt the shared dropdown primitives instead of hand-rolling incompatible ones
statement: Four incompatible hand-rolled dropdowns coexist in one pocket, one with NO dismissal path at all, while shared primitives (useClickOutside, useViewportClampAbsolute, Listbox) sit unadopted. Portal-anchored plus close-on-scroll/resize is the good local example to converge on.

title: Let an icon primitive downgrade display modes its content can't survive
statement: An icon primitive should silently DOWNGRADE display modes its content kind can't survive (pop-out rendering is fine for curated SVGs/emoji but blobs fallback icons and full-bleed uploads → downgrade those kinds to framed). Both renderers delegate classification to one resolver; hooks are called unconditionally with null to respect rules-of-hooks.

title: Preview a theme by re-scoping CSS variables and painting from its advertised samples
statement: Preview a theme by re-scoping CSS variables under data-theme; paint each tile from the theme's advertised sample colors via inline styles so every tile previews ITS OWN theme regardless of cascade timing; crossfade keyed on a hash of the visible variables.

title: Advance on the user's real click with capture+once over a pass-through highlight
statement: Universal click-to-advance uses {capture:true, once:true} over a pointer-events-none highlight so the same click performs the real action AND advances, and can never double-advance. holdForClick suspends auto-advance only when the step has a real anchor (an anchorless hold step keeps its timer so it can't hard-stall); manual navigation auto-pauses; keyboard controls read live state via getState() so they bind once per walkthrough.

title: Name forward vs seed as two distinct primitives for handing off a composed message
statement: Handing a composed message to an assistant has two named primitives: forward (fire now — surface a fallback orb/panel so it's never invisible, fresh conversation per forwarded ask with a documented never-drop fallback, immediate scripted spoken ack, rides the always-mounted consumer) and seed (fill the composer and wait).

title: Enforce two communication dimensions and delete the third
statement: Companion communication is architecturally two dimensions — orb for quick state/decision, chat for full information — with the third (popover) deleted. One-shot reactions get a durable counterpart (unreadReplies + preview), the badge is cleared in exactly ONE place, autonomous actions accumulate into a bounded in-session ledger rather than a 10s toast, and the decision queue stays un-gated because a gated queue would make pending approvals invisible outside their own pages.

title: Keep the attention taxonomy in one pure vocabulary module
statement: A two-level attention taxonomy lives in one pure vocabulary module: an ordered kind tuple that IS the render order, an EMPTY_ constant, a type guard, severity buckets where unmapped kinds fall to nudges rather than inventing urgency, and an isCountableNudge predicate so aggregated rows are neither rendered nor counted twice.

title: Scope nested-palette keyboard ownership and share the exact filter with the parent
statement: A nested palette owns Arrow/Enter/Escape only while open AND at least one preset survives the filter — a no-match state can't trap keys — and exports the identical filter so the parent mirrors the child's logic; the index clamps when the filter shrinks and focus defers to rAF after seeding. Drafts seed local state once, write back per keystroke, rehydrate via a prevConversationIdRef on thread switch, and setDraft skips clearing an already-blank draft.

title: Make one ordered as-const tuple the whole vocabulary, every map a total Record
statement: One ordered `as const` tuple is the entire vocabulary and every derived map is a total Record keyed off it: adding or removing a dimension is a compile error at every render site, iteration order is identical across surfaces, and labels are labelKeys typed into Translations, resolved at render.

title: Give the registry an optional bespoke-art slot whose structural marker survives absent data
statement: An optional bespoke art slot on the registry keeps the "structural marker stays even when data is absent" contract: custom art uses currentColor, iconOpacity hides only the inner icon, per-dim decoration composes over the base, hideBase exists for the one dim replacing base geometry, and everything shares a fixed viewBox scaled by size.

title: Put a structural row contract between N producers and one renderer
statement: A structural row contract (GlyphRow) is the single seam between N producers and one renderer: the doc names the three producers, and a tri-state presence value (linked|shared|none) lets one petal render three bodies.

title: Use a generic grid with per-row render props instead of branching the card
statement: Instead of branching the card component per mode, a generic grid takes per-row render props and slots; mode drives only chrome, keeping the layout "data-shaped, not state-shaped" (scaled to a layout with 11 documented slots and an ASCII diagram).

title: Derive emptiness from the render descriptor, never a hand-synced parallel switch
statement: A parallel isDimEmpty switch hand-synced with the render switch ("Mirrors the switch below; keep the two in sync") is a drift trap — derive emptiness from the same per-dim descriptor the renderer uses.

title: Namespace every SVG defs id with a per-instance uid
statement: Every SVG defs id (patterns, gradients, filters) is namespaced by a per-instance uid derived from data identity, because many sigils render per page and colliding ids silently cross-wire their defs.

title: Drive a texture-per-dimension CVD fallback off the same registry as the colors
statement: Color-vision-deficiency support (WCAG 1.4.1) is a texture per dimension driven off the same registry as the hues — 8 micro-textures selected by dimension INDEX, tinted with a light wash so residual hue survives — wired only when the theme store's cvdSafe flag is on.

title: Pass CSS custom properties into SVG through style, not presentation attributes
statement: CSS custom properties in SVG must go through style, not presentation attributes (stopColor via style so var(--primary) resolves); status colors ride var(--status-*) + color-mix so theme calibration and CVD remap apply automatically, while deliberately-neutral colors stay literal hex.

title: Overlay absolutely-positioned HTML icons on SVG from the cached geometry
statement: A hybrid of SVG art plus an absolutely-positioned HTML icon overlay gets tooltips and theme colouring without SVG text handling; overlay positions come from the same cached geometry, with per-presence radius/box precomputed.

title: Stack overlay totems center-out and opt tiles back into pointer events
statement: Overlay totems stack center-out (0,-1,+1,-2,+2) with the container pointer-events-none spanning the card and tiles opting back in — the old title= tooltip never fired because hover couldn't reach the tiles — and the overflow +N tile's tooltip lists the hidden names.

title: Give a radial SVG group roving tabindex with parent-owned key routing
statement: A radial SVG control gets roving tabindex with parent-owned key routing: one petal is the tab stop, Arrow/Home/End move it, the handler is created once and re-bound with the dim in the child so memo stays effective, and the keyboard focus ring is drawn as an extra path because SVG outline rendering is unreliable. The same shape recurs in a tablist with automatic activation and a fallback tab stop.

title: Return focus only when nothing real holds it
statement: Focus return must refuse to STEAL focus: return to the originating element only if activeElement is null or body — skip when focus already landed somewhere real.

title: Use role=region for non-modal overlays and record the reason at the call site
statement: Non-modal overlays take role="region", not dialog, with the reason recorded at the call site: no backdrop and no trap make dialog semantics wrong, while the overlay still takes focus on mount and handles Escape with stopPropagation.

title: Make the legend a coverage key with shared hover state
statement: The legend doubles as a coverage key — it names all dimensions at once with presence encoded in dot fill (solid/faint/hollow) — and shares hover state with the main control so hovering either surface lights both.

title: Consolidate an icon map into one canonical module that records its reconciliation
statement: When consolidating a duplicated icon map into a single source of truth across surfaces, record the reconciliation in the doc: enumerate each icon change and which pre-existing copy won, and keep explicit fallbacks for unknown types.

title: Own keys exclusively through a priority registry, tested as nothing-beneath-is-called
statement: Keyboard ownership goes through a registry with a priority ladder whose neighbours are named, and the claim is exclusivity, not just priority — "a key the deck ignores must not reach an invisible surface either," tested as nothing-beneath-is-called with symmetric unmount and yields-to-above cases. A DANGEROUS_KEYS table annotates what each key does on each surface; deliberate choices include vertical keys reserved for reading, `U` instead of mod+Z (exclusivity would swallow undo in a text box), and recoverFocus because every verdict remounts the top card.

title: Collapse mixed backend detail blobs to prose-or-facts, bailing to prose on any ambiguity
statement: Normalize a field that arrives in several shapes (free prose, key=value lists, JSON, raw error text) through tiered parsers into one predictable prose-or-facts union, where any parse ambiguity degrades to prose (nothing lost) and pretty JSON is preserved separately for a power-user 'show raw' affordance.

title: Anchor score charts to the metric's fixed scale, never the sample's min/max
statement: When a score has a bounded scale (0-5, 0-100), project sparklines and distributions onto that fixed range rather than auto-scaling to the visible sample, so the same value sits at the same vertical position on every row and trends stay comparable across entities at a glance.

title: Take pointer capture only after drag slop, and swallow the trailing click
statement: On a pannable canvas with clickable nodes, capturing the pointer on pointerdown retargets the entire pointer stream — including the eventual click — at the canvas, so node clicks never fire and every tap reads as background. Capture only once movement exceeds a small slop (~3px), and after a real pan ends set a one-shot flag consumed in a capture-phase click handler so releasing a drag over a node doesn't select it. Any manual gesture also cancels an in-flight animated camera move — the user always wins the camera.

title: Bind wheel-zoom as a native non-passive listener on the drawing element, not its container
statement: Two documented failure modes in one listener choice: React's synthetic onWheel is passive by default, so a zoom that cannot preventDefault scrolls the page underneath on every notch — it must be a native addEventListener('wheel', fn, { passive: false }). And it must live on the SVG itself, not the wrapping container: overlays (modals, side rails) are DOM children of the container and wheel bubbling follows the DOM, so a container-level listener turns every scroll inside an overlay into a canvas zoom.

title: Zero-fill every date-by-series cell when pivoting long rows for stacked charts
statement: Pivoting a long-format time series (one row per date x series) into wide rows for a stacked area/bar chart must zero-fill every missing (date, series) cell after collecting the full series set — a key absent from one row renders as undefined, which produces NaN tooltips and visual jumps in stacked geometry. Sum duplicates for the same cell rather than overwriting, and sort dates ascending on the way out.

title: Pause toast lifetimes on hover AND on tab-background, re-anchoring the clock on resume
statement: A toast's auto-dismiss timer must pause while hovered and while the document is hidden (or timers silently burn through their duration off-screen), and resuming must re-anchor the tick clock to now so the paused interval is never counted as elapsed. Keep the visible progress bar CSS-driven (animation + a data-paused attribute + a --duration custom property) so pause/resume stays smooth; JS owns only the dismiss decision and the label.

title: Cap every ambient indicator set and collapse the excess into one +N counter
statement: Any unbounded ambient surface — toast stacks, orbiting activity dots, capacity strips — needs a visible-count cap with the overflow collapsed into a single "+N" element, so the chrome stays legible under load and the user still knows the total. Sort by priority before slicing so the cap drops the least important items.

title: Bind semantic spacing tokens to density CSS variables so one setting reflows every card
statement: Express card padding and section gaps as semantic tokens whose values are CSS custom properties set by an app-wide density setting (`p-[var(--density-pad)]`), with the default resolving to the historical values so appearance is unchanged out of the box. Deliberately exempt surfaces that should not breathe with density (modal chrome bands) and document the exemption on the token.

title: Require a movement threshold before a resize handle commits a width
statement: A drag-resize divider must ignore sub-threshold pointer movement (~3px) so a plain click never freezes a flexible `minmax(…,1fr)` column at its current pixel width, and must persist the width only if a real drag happened.

title: Under a global MotionConfig, must-run animations use CSS keyframes, not framer
statement: An app-level `<MotionConfig reducedMotion={visible ? 'user' : 'always'}>` snaps EVERY framer animation (opacity included) when set to 'always' — silently killing reveals that must still play. Animations that must run regardless (or that need their own reduced-motion policy) belong in CSS keyframes, which MotionConfig does not govern; document the guard in the preset library so nobody reintroduces framer variants. When sequencing an ambient loop after an entrance, fill it `forwards` — `both` applies the loop's from-state during the start delay and fights the entrance.

title: Replay a viewport-entry animation with IntersectionObserver plus a run key, skipping the first observation
statement: To replay an entrance animation whenever an element re-enters the viewport without double-playing on mount, keep a `seen` ref that records the initial observation without firing, and bump a `runKey` (remounting the animated subtree) only on a genuine hidden→visible transition.

title: Guard display:contents wrappers against the 0×0 bounding rect
statement: Chromium/WebView2 returns a zero rect from `getBoundingClientRect()` on a box-less (`display: contents`) wrapper, which pins anything positioned from it (tooltips, popovers) to the viewport's top-left. Detect the 0×0 rect and fall back to the wrapped child's real box.

title: Put aria-sort on the column-header element and swap the tag for grid faux tables
statement: A sortable header primitive must place `aria-sort` on the element with the columnheader role — `<th>` implicitly, or an explicit `role="columnheader"` div for CSS-grid faux tables — and give the sort button a full next-action label. Verify every claim with tests, and lean on a global reduced-motion CSS reset instead of a per-component gate for the caret transition.

title: Give shared primitives label FUNCTIONS, not translation keys
statement: A domain-agnostic primitive stays i18n-free by accepting labels as functions — e.g. `summary: (group, count) => string` — so interpolation and the i18n import live in the (translated) caller. The primitive never learns about the catalog, and the pure model beneath it stays React-free and generic over row type via injected accessors.

title: scale-* transforms do not resize the layout box — size illustrations with real dimensions
statement: A transform-scaled element still measures its pre-transform size: a `scale-[3.25]` watermark measured 48px while painting 156px, overflowing onto the heading. Give illustrations a real layout box (`w-24 h-24`) and choose deliberately which element yields under pressure — withhold `shrink-0` from the art and grant it to the heading, so a short pane clips the picture, never the message.

title: Replay a CSS keyframe with the remove-class → force-reflow → re-add idiom, once per codebase
statement: The only reliable way to re-trigger a CSS animation is: remove the class, force a reflow (`void el.offsetWidth`), re-add the class, and clean up on `animationend { once: true }`. Codify it as one exported helper/hook — this repo factored the same idiom four ways (a hook, an exported helper, and two inline copies), which is the argument for sanctioning a single implementation.

title: Build skeletons as explicit twins: copied chrome classes, em-sized bars inside real typo line boxes
statement: A loading skeleton earns zero layout shift by being a maintained TWIN of the real component: deliberately COPY the real class list (with an in-file instruction to update the twin in the same change — sharing would couple styling refactors), size placeholder bars in `em` INSIDE the real `typo-*` line boxes so height is truthful, and default to a calm variant (static, low-contrast, no pulse). Table skeletons take a column spec mirroring the real grid, plus a stacked mobile variant.

title: Suffix every framer layoutId with a per-instance useId
statement: Two mounted instances of a component sharing a literal `layoutId` make the shared-layout indicator teleport/animate BETWEEN the instances. Namespace every layoutId with a per-instance `useId()` suffix — this repo enforces it independently in four components, which is the tell that it belongs in review checklists.

title: Never nest interactive elements — render secondary actions as siblings or role-button spans
statement: Nesting a real control inside a `<button>` is invalid HTML, breaks hydration, and the inner control swallows the outer's click. Render a card/row action as a SIBLING of the toggle button; when a clickable must live visually inside a button (orbit dots on a sidebar button), use a `span role="button" tabIndex={0}` with Enter/Space handling and stopPropagation instead of a nested `<button>`.

title: Unlayered token classes beat Tailwind utilities — change the token, not the call site
statement: When a design system ships its typography as unlayered CSS classes (`typo-*`), local Tailwind utility overrides silently lose the cascade: a `font-normal`/opacity patch applied at a call site has no effect at all. The durable fix for a styling change is editing the token definition, and the failed-patch history is worth recording at the site that tempted it.

title: Scroll-spy binds the real scroll parent up-front and never gates on current overflow
statement: A section scroll-spy must walk ancestors for `overflow-y: auto|scroll|overlay` (window fallback) at bind time and deliberately NOT check `scrollHeight > clientHeight` — content often grows after mount (async panels), so gating on current overflow permanently disables the spy. Memoize per-id callback-ref setters so tagging a section never churns the ref, and compute container-relative jump deltas rather than scrollIntoView when a scroll parent exists.

title: Lazy-load libraries that inspect child identity via one render-prop wrapper, not per-component React.lazy
statement: Libraries like recharts match children by component identity (`child.type === Bar`), so wrapping each export in its own `React.lazy` silently breaks composition — the Suspense wrapper fails the identity check. Use one dynamic import for the whole library exposed through a render-prop wrapper: a single shared chunk, and normal child composition inside the callback.

title: Namespace drag payloads by custom MIME and clear drag state on drop, not only dragend
statement: Kanban-style drag needs three guards: a custom MIME type so foreign drags are inert and `dragOver` can reject before preventDefault; `dragLeave` ignoring bubbles from descendants via relatedTarget containment; and clearing the dragging id in `onDrop` — when the drop moves the card to another column, the source element unmounts before its native `dragend` ever fires, leaving the moved card stuck at drag opacity.

title: Keep a rAF loop alive across prop changes by calling the tick through a ref
statement: If a driver effect schedules `requestAnimationFrame(tick)` directly, it must depend on `tick` — whose identity changes whenever its inputs change — cancelling and failing to reschedule the loop mid-run. Store the latest tick in a ref the loop calls through, so the driver effect's deps stay stable and the animation survives estimate/prop updates. Pair with an honest progress model: linear to ~85% over the estimate, asymptotic crawl to ~98%, an over-estimate warning state, and 100% only on real completion.

title: Virtualize streaming logs with threshold-based sticky-bottom and typed pre-output states
statement: A live log panel should virtualize variable-height lines (measureElement), decide auto-scroll stickiness by a small bottom-distance threshold (~10px), show a jump-to-bottom affordance with an unseen-line counter only when the user has scrolled away, and replace the single generic empty state with a typed one — idle / connecting / queued-with-position / failed — because "no output yet" means different things.

title: Normalize repeated human decisions onto one record type and one action control, with tone rationale recorded
statement: When several features grow accept/reject queues, unify them on one domain-free DecisionRecord/DecisionTone vocabulary and one actions component whose closed tone map makes a fourth tone impossible to invent. Record the interaction rationale, not just styling — e.g. reject stays visually quiet until hover because "a destructive-looking reject button makes reviewers hesitate on a queue they are supposed to burn down", and "the row opens; the buttons decide".

title: Keep security-reassurance badges live, control-free, and honest about their own gaps
statement: A green 'vault secured' badge is a display, never a control (no 'encrypt now' button — the guarantee is automatic); it must reflect the actual variant in force (keychain vs machine-derived fallback), flip amber when a subsidiary guarantee fails (missed audit writes), and stay live via a slow poll plus refresh-on-focus — a mount-only fetch left it permanently green through a live failure.

title: Every zoom level of an aggregate must reduce from one module so the bands cannot disagree
statement: When a view renders the same underlying data at multiple detail levels (far count, mid breakdown, near full detail), all levels must reduce from ONE pure module — 'a mid breakdown that did not add up to the far count would make one of the two bands a liar, and the operator zooms between them.' Corollaries: filter dead items in the shared module (not at call sites) so no band counts finished work; KEEP unrecognized states rather than dropping them ('an unrecognised state is still a running thing'); and render empty lanes as empty lanes, never omit them — 'a missing lane and a zero-count lane look identical once they are gone.'

title: Spatial keyboard navigation: one roving cursor with cone-scored directional picks and a nearest fallback
statement: A spatial map must not become N tab stops ('a 200-project portfolio must not become 200 tab presses') — use one roving cursor and let arrow keys navigate spatially: candidates must sit inside a cone around the direction vector, scored by along-axis distance plus weighted lateral drift so 'right' prefers the item actually beside you over a nearer one off-axis. When the cone is empty, fall back to plain-nearest so a sparse or single-column map can never trap the cursor with no way out. Keep the geometry pure (no React/DOM) so the decision logic is unit-testable.

title: Lock grid tile order to creation time with a total tie-break; tiles leave only by explicit dismissal
statement: In an operator-facing grid of long-lived work units, spatial stability is a contract: order is locked to creation time (never activity), with the id as a total tie-break so equal timestamps cannot reshuffle between fetches, exited/parked units render as in-place tombstones, a resumed unit inherits the old row's creation timestamp so it keeps its slot, and a tile disappears exactly one way — the operator dismisses it. Destructive controls are state-aware: the same button kills a live unit (leaving a tombstone) and dismisses a tombstone.

title: Derive layout jitter and placeholder metrics from a hash of the stable id, and flag simulated rows as simulated
statement: Anything decorative-but-rebuilt — radial jitter in a graph layout, placeholder stats for rows with no real data yet — must come from a deterministic hash (FNV-1a) of the entity's stable id, never Math.random: a rebuild must not reshuffle the field under the reader's cursor, and a re-render must not change a placeholder number. When placeholder values stand in for missing real data, carry an explicit simulated flag so the UI can mark them, and keep genuinely-measured fields (state, age, screen health) real even on simulated rows.

title: Cluster feed rows by consecutive run of a shared key, anchored at the newest event — never globally by id
statement: When folding a flat activity feed into a readable conversation, collapse only CONSECUTIVE items sharing a cluster key (assignment id, thread id) into one row, anchored at the cluster's newest timestamp. Two bursts of the same key separated by other traffic stay two rows — because that is how a conversation actually reads. Keep the unclustered flat log as a separate surface rather than a mode of the same one.

title: Compute each facet's counts against the rows surviving the OTHER dimensions
statement: In a multi-dimension faceted filter rail, count each dimension's values against the rows that survive every other active dimension — not against the global unfiltered set and not against the fully filtered set. A count then answers 'selecting this shows N rows given what you're already looking at', which is the only reading that makes the rail a browsing instrument rather than a misleading total.

title: Document-level hotkey layers: skip modifiers and ALL typing contexts (including hidden helper textareas), and narrow the active set per overlay
statement: A document-level single-key hotkey layer must bail on any modifier chord and on any typing context — matching input, textarea, select, AND contenteditable, which also covers embedded widgets' hidden helper textareas (xterm.js) so keys typed into a focused terminal never trigger navigation. Gate the whole layer on an enabled flag (modal open = off), narrow the active key set when an overlay is up, and read handlers through a ref so the listener attaches once.

title: Fullscreen overlays: reserve chrome space in layout, not z-order, and portal above transformed ancestors
statement: Two stacking traps for app-wide overlays: (1) an ancestor with `contain: layout` scopes descendants' z-index to that subtree, so 'the footer has a higher z-index' silently stops being true for a body-portaled overlay — reserve the footer's space in the overlay's layout (explicit bottom offset) instead of overlapping and trusting z-order; (2) `position: fixed` inside a transform-using ancestor (framer-motion layout animations) positions relative to that ancestor, not the viewport — portal the overlay to document.body.

title: Split a mixed lifecycle enum into orthogonal display axes at the UI edge
statement: A single backend lifecycle enum often conflates orthogonal questions (is the process alive? what is the work doing?). Rather than widening the enum or rendering one ambiguous badge, derive the axes in a pure exhaustive-switch function at the UI edge and render one compact indicator per axis. Export the per-axis palette records so the legend renders the exact same tokens, and let downstream aggregate surfaces (lane tallies, footers) read a single shared lane mapping so a state can never sit in one lane on one surface and another elsewhere.

title: Cover unbounded async waits with a three-phase choreography whose payoff is triggered by real data, never a timer
statement: For a single long backend call with no intermediate signal (50-155s+ LLM turn), model the loading UI as bounded-intro -> infinite self-sustaining hold -> payoff, where the determinate progress bar fills only through the bounded phase, swaps to an indeterminate shimmer for the hold, and the emotional peak fires the instant real data streams in. Fields that have not arrived render skeletons, never placeholder lies — the animation converts unavoidable latency into product value with zero invented data.

title: Fast-forward an animation on early completion — never cut it — and pace burst data into a timed reveal
statement: When the backend finishes before the animation, compress the remainder into a fixed-length sprint by recomputing the step interval from the remaining items, and delay the handoff so the payoff actually plays. The inverse mechanic: when a burst of results lands at once, a generic useTimedReveal(items, interval, immediate) slices the array forward one item per beat via a self-cancelling setTimeout chain keyed on state, with an immediate escape hatch for the fast-forward path.

title: Surface one ranked resume signal, never a list — priority-ordered kinds with null meaning render nothing
statement: A 'continue where you left off' affordance should resolve to at most ONE signal via an explicit priority ladder over a typed union (e.g. fresh failure > paused guided flow > last edit), returning null when nothing clears the bar so the surface renders nothing rather than filler. Within a rank, pick the most recent explicitly (sort, not `find()`, when source order is unguaranteed) and clamp future-dated timestamps from clock skew before age checks. Each kind carries its own dismiss semantics.

title: Seed cosmetic variety from a stable hash plus the date, not Math.random
statement: For a rotating cosmetic choice (hero background, accent variant), derive the pick from `hash(stableUserKey) + dayOfYear()` modulo the option count instead of Math.random. The user still gets variety (new day → new look) but the choice is stable within a day, which removes per-mount flicker on theme toggles, HMR reloads, and navigation back to the surface. A tiny FNV-1a is enough — the hash needs stability, not cryptography.

title: Steps with no detectable action complete on explicit acknowledgement, never a timer
statement: In a guided flow, steps whose completion is a real app event auto-complete on that event; purely informational steps (look at a dashboard, watch a stream) must complete on an explicit 'I've explored this' button — never a hidden timer. Which steps are acknowledgement-style is declared as data (a listed set of completion-event keys), so adding one is a registry edit and the panel renders the button automatically.

title: In a measurement matrix, synthesize placeholder rows so unmeasured entities — especially the live config — stay visible and actionable
statement: A version-by-model matrix built only from measured rows hides exactly the rows users must act on: the currently-live configuration that has no score yet, and versions never measured at all. Synthesize a placeholder row for the active (version, model) when it is unmeasured, and one null-model placeholder per otherwise-rowless version, then order active-first, measured-by-score, placeholders last.

title: Clamp the gauge, print the true number when a metric can legitimately exceed its nominal scale
statement: Some scored dimensions legitimately exceed 100 (bonus completions, over-achievement). Clamp only the visual bar width to the scale so layout never breaks, but render the real value as the label — silently capping the number hides the over-achievement, and letting the bar overflow breaks the chart.

title: Honor reduced-motion with a real render branch to plain DOM, not by zeroing animation durations
statement: Zeroed durations still mount the animation library's wrappers, still schedule its effects, and can still flash. When prefers-reduced-motion is set, branch to a plain element tree that never imports motion wrappers for that render, and also skip derived motion props like per-row animationDelay so stagger math cannot reintroduce movement.

title: Explain a disabled control through a focusable wrapper
statement: A native `disabled` button swallows pointer and focus events, so neither hover tooltips nor keyboard focus can surface *why* it is disabled. Give the primitive a `disabledReason` prop that wraps it in a focusable (tabIndex=0, aria-disabled) span carrying the tooltip, the not-allowed cursor, the focus ring, and the button's layout footprint.

title: Queue and re-key live-region announcements so none are lost
statement: Live-region announcements pushed in the same tick collapse: React coalesces the setState calls and only the last message reaches the DOM. And an identical consecutive message is not re-announced at all. Queue announcements, flush one per interval, and bump a key on the live-region node so each message gets its own commit and its own utterance.

title: Ship a tablist with roving tabindex and arrow-key navigation
statement: Adding `role="tablist"`/`role="tab"` changes what assistive tech and keyboard users expect: only the active tab belongs in the Tab order, and Arrow/Home/End move between tabs — skipping disabled ones. Build it into the shared tab primitive so no feature has to remember it, and give each instance its own layout id so animated indicators don't teleport between bars.

title: Give every dashboard number a healthy range and a destination
statement: Raw metrics are not actionable. Attach to each KPI what it means, what a healthy value looks like, and where clicking it goes; translate engineer-facing severity tokens into plain-language urgency and next-step guidance; and carry every severity in a second, non-colour channel (shape/icon) so the signal survives colour-blindness and greyscale.

title: Format metrics to survive both extremes of their range
statement: Metric text has predictable failure modes at both ends of the range. Use tabular/lining figures so digits do not jitter as values update; compact large counts but attach the exact value as a title only when compaction actually hid digits; clamp absurd percentages; and floor tiny nonzero costs to a '<' form so a real spend never renders as $0.00.

title: Replace N modal booleans with one typed modal stack
statement: A screen with several dialogs accumulates a `useState` pair and a handler per dialog, and loses z-ordering. Model the open dialogs as a stack of discriminated-union entries with `open` / `close(type?)` / `replace` / `closeAll` plus typed `find` and `isOpen` — adding a dialog then costs one union member and zero state variables.

title: Bind a destructive confirm to the target it was raised against
statement: A confirm dialog for a destructive operation is a promise about a specific target. If the user can switch that target while the dialog is open — different credential, different database, different tab — clear the pending action. Pin the executor closure captured at submit time in a ref, clear the pending action when that identity changes, and re-check it synchronously on confirm to close the click race.

title: Extract anchored-portal positioning into one shared hook
statement: Every menu or popover portalled out of its container needs the same work: measure the anchor, re-measure on scroll (including scrollable ancestors) and resize, and flip when there is no room below. Write that geometry once as a hook that returns a position and a flip decision, and let each overlay decide only its own chrome.

title: Derive every primitive's classes from one shared token hook
statement: With a small fixed set of themes and no component library, put every primitive's class strings behind a single token hook that branches on the theme once; each primitive then consumes named tokens instead of owning styling logic. Know the ceiling this buys: a third theme means touching every token, which is the signal to move to a real token file.

title: Keep the shared catalog domain-free, and let a lint rule enforce it
statement: A primitives catalog stays reusable only if its components cannot reach into features or domain data — everything they need must arrive through props. Scope an import restriction to the catalog directory so the boundary is machine-checked; a convention stated only in a README erodes within a few sprints.

title: Add to a shared primitive behind an isolated, opt-in render path
statement: When a primitive already has dozens of consumers, do not thread a new capability through the shared branch. Make each addition opt-in via a prop that is a no-op when absent, and if the feature changes structure, mount a separate sub-component for it — then state the invariant in the code: the default path is unchanged.

title: Express theme variance in CSS, not by reading the theme store
statement: When a component's light/dark difference is purely presentational, emit a `[data-theme=…]` rule (or use a token that inverts) instead of subscribing to the theme. The component stays importable from anywhere with no store dependency, and switching themes repaints without re-rendering it.

title: Pin a virtualized group header through the range extractor
statement: To pin a group header in a virtualizer, override the range extractor to always include the nearest header at-or-above the viewport top, and store which one is active in a ref rather than state — the virtualizer already re-renders on scroll, and a setState inside the extractor is a render loop. Share the extractor, the header component and the flattening helper so every grouped surface pins identically.

title: Compose cold-load UX from four shared mechanics, never a per-page skeleton
statement: For any async surface, do not build a bespoke skeleton or spinner. Compose four shared mechanics: (1) a delayed header-only RouteChunkSkeleton as the lazy-route Suspense fallback (kills the blank chunk-load gap, invisible when the chunk is warm); (2) ghost-under-permanent-chrome gated `isLoading && items.length === 0` so a fetch never hides rendered data; (3) an id-guarded RevealItem/useRevealTracker entrance cascade (one-shot, first-viewport, reduced-motion aware); (4) a module-scoped warm cache so a remount paints last-known data instead of re-ghosting. This is the full doctrine that the single existing 'delay lives on the placeholder' item is only law 3 of.

title: Show ghost placeholders only into cold emptiness, never over rendered rows
statement: Gate ghost placeholders on isFetching && rows.length===0: never hide rows already on screen, never flash empty state mid-fetch. Ghosts reuse real row geometry with a 120ms animation-delay and fill-mode both.

title: Page transcripts by keyset with a derived cursor and re-arming exhaustion
statement: Keyset transcript pagination derives its cursor from the oldest loaded message, not state, so it stays correct across wholesale refetches; a carry cursor handles all-filtered pages (valid only while its anchor is still oldest, inner loop bounded per gesture); exhaustion is stored AS THE ID it was proven against so paging re-arms when the anchor moves; an in-flight thread switch is discarded; scroll restores by exactly scrollHeight - prevHeight in rAF.

title: Split a schedule timeline at 'now': project the future, but ground the past only in run records
statement: A calendar/timeline for scheduled work must never render past occurrences from the same projection that draws the future — past slots are matched against real execution records and unmatched slots render as 'unknown', revealing skips, rate-limits and downtime instead of faking successes.

title: Union-merge partially-overlapping queries so the headline signal always renders its own row
statement: When a panel joins two queries that have different limits and filters (so neither covers the other), merge by union and let the signal-side row render from its own fields when the primary list never loaded it — dropping it because the other page is short would rebuild the very bug the panel exists to expose.

title: Build filter vocabularies from a registry unioned with observed rows
statement: A type/category filter over an event stream should offer the union of a server-side known-vocabulary registry (curated seed plus every type ever observed) and the types present in currently loaded rows — the registry lets users filter for a type before any matching row has loaded, and loaded rows backfill brand-new types the registry hasn't refreshed yet.

title: Lazy-gate an optional module's fetch cluster on its anchor entity — but explicit routes must still resolve ready
statement: When an optional feature (not seeded on every install/tier) has both an always-mounted teaser and an explicitly navigated page sharing one data hook, give the hook a `lazy` option: teaser callers wait for the feature's anchor entity to be confirmed present (derived from already-loaded state, no extra IPC) before firing the fetch cluster; the explicit route stays eager because it must resolve `ready` even when the anchor is absent, so it renders an empty state instead of hanging on a spinner forever.

title: Every badge owns its own poll registration — never ride another surface's ticker
statement: A count badge that stays fresh only because some OTHER component happens to poll the same store is a latent bug: collapse that component and the badge freezes at a stale number. Register the badge's own refresh on the shared polling coordinator's bucket (so it coalesces with everyone else's tick instead of adding a private setInterval on its own offset).

title: Invalidate the downstream fetch cache, not just the selection, when a parent picker changes
statement: In dependent/chained pickers, clearing child selections is insufficient — the fetch effect's 'already cached, skip' guard keeps serving items scoped to the old parent. Delete the cached child entries too.

title: Flag saved selections as stale only after a confirmed successful fetch
statement: Compute 'this saved pick no longer exists' only once a real response has arrived — computing during loading or after an error marks every pick stale on a transient blip. Offer an explicit one-click 'drop stale' instead of silently pruning.

title: A per-key cache-hit short-circuit blinds the store to set changes — compare a set signature too
statement: Skipping a refetch because every key is already cached permanently hides additions, removals and backend-side changes once each id has been seen once. Also compare a sorted-id signature against the last successful fetch, and prune cache entries for ids no longer present.

title: A reusable stream consumer must let the caller opt out of its internal buffer
statement: When a generic streaming hook keeps its own bounded line buffer and a consumer pipes the same lines into an external store, the same stream is buffered twice with divergent trim points. Expose an explicit opt-out (bufferLines: false) so exactly one owner holds the data, and read the flag through a ref so the listener closure sees updates without destabilizing the start callback's identity.

title: Refcount channel subscriptions and key effect dependencies by value, not array identity
statement: When N surfaces watch the same live feed, route them through one refcounted subscription in the store: the first subscriber triggers the fetch, a shared service keeps every subscribed channel fresh, and each surface releases on unmount — instead of each running its own poll + push listener. In the React hook, join the id array into a string key for the effect dependency because 'callers routinely pass fresh arrays' — subscribing by identity would churn the subscription every render.

title: Let shared data hooks take feed opt-in flags, and make bounded reads report that they are bounded
statement: A hook that fuses several polled feeds for its home surface gets reused by leaner surfaces that render only one of them — and then everyone pays for all the pollers. Give the hook per-feed opt-in flags whose defaults preserve the original surface's behavior unchanged. When a caller opts into a row cap on an otherwise-unbounded read, return a hasMore flag with the rows: a capped list that does not say it is capped is the same lie as a failed read that renders as empty.

title: Register stream listeners before invoking the command — and unhook them if the world moved during the await
statement: In an event-driven start flow, register progress AND status listeners first (in one Promise.all), then invoke the backend command — a fast completion can emit before late-registered listeners exist. After the registration await resolves, re-check the generation counter: if a cancel/reset/newer start happened meanwhile, immediately unhook the just-registered listeners instead of storing them.

title: Type the stream outcome as the backend's three-way result — a question is neither a result nor an error
statement: When the backend pipeline can end a round with Result | Question | Failed, mirror that three-way shape in the frontend hook's typed outcome so a clarifying question doesn't get smuggled through the result or error channel. Default the question type to never and collapse the outcome back to the original two-way union byte-for-byte (via [T] extends [never] to dodge conditional-type distribution), so existing consumers' annotations keep type-checking unchanged.

title: Layer AI-task hooks: one stream primitive, one task wrapper, thin domain hooks naming only events and phases
statement: Structure streaming-AI frontends as three layers: a generic stream hook (listeners, generation guard, timeout, bounded lines), a task wrapper that absorbs the recurring boilerplate (default line extraction, standard status resolution, cancel absorption, tracing), and per-domain hooks that supply nothing but event names, phase names, and start/cancel functions. New AI flows then cost ~20 declarative lines instead of a re-implemented state machine.

title: Extract a multi-step apply as a dependency-injected transaction returning typed failed operations
statement: A 'apply this AI result' flow that updates an entity plus creates N side entities (triggers, subscriptions) should be a standalone function taking its store actions as injected deps — decoupled from the streaming machinery so template adoption, import, and batch paths reuse it. It returns warnings plus a typed FailedOperation list that carries each failed item's ORIGINAL payload, so the UI can offer selective retry of exactly the failed subset.

title: A fetch-if-empty guard keyed on the empty result loops forever — latch the request in a ref
statement: `useEffect(() => { if (list.length === 0) fetch(); }, [list])` is an infinite loop on genuinely-empty data: every fetch of an empty collection produces a fresh `[]` identity, which re-produces the guard state. Latch 'already requested' in a one-shot ref instead. Sibling trap: keying an unrelated fetch on a refetched array's identity re-runs it on every rename/background refresh — fetch once on mount if the data doesn't actually depend on the array.

title: Pause a persisted surface's refresh loop while a transient overlay owns it
statement: When a transient overlay (contextual view, briefing) is projected over a surface that normally fetches persisted state on mount + window focus, the fetch/refresh loop must be suspended for the overlay's lifetime — otherwise a background refetch clobbers the overlay with older persisted content. The event that publishes NEW persisted content explicitly drops the overlay and refetches, encoding 'persisted just changed → overlay is obsolete'. Dismissing the overlay restores the persisted view untouched.

title: A filter wired only into the primary backend query silently no-ops on views fed from a different source — apply the facet at every source
statement: When one surface renders data from two sources (a filtered backend query for the main view, a precomputed summary for a secondary view), filter controls wired only into the query become dead controls on the secondary view: the dropdown and clickable tiles render, do nothing, and raise no error. Apply the active facet client-side to every source the surface renders, and sort before filtering so filtering preserves the established order.

title: Give every entity one hook module owning its client and its cache
statement: Route all entity CRUD through per-entity modules that export both the API client and the query hooks built on it, so cache keys, invalidation and optimistic updates live beside the calls they govern. Old import paths can survive as thin re-export shims rather than forcing a repo-wide rename.

title: Keep a run-once backfill effect's deps empty, or it wipes live state
statement: Effects that seed a buffer which a live subscription then owns must have empty (or genuinely minimal) deps. Adding a collection the effect body doesn't read — because a render-time helper reads it — re-runs the seed on every unrelated mutation of that collection and throws away everything the subscription accumulated. Where a dep is genuinely needed, key on a derived signature of only the fields that matter and read the object through a ref.

title: Render a merged feed only down to the horizon every source loaded
statement: When a single scrollable feed k-way-merges pages from N sources, rendering everything you have lets a shallower source's older rows appear ABOVE the user's scroll position on the next page. Compute the horizon — the deepest timestamp every source has loaded past — render only at or above it, and make loadMore deepen the shallowest source.

title: Tombstone deleted ids so an in-flight fetch can't resurrect them
statement: Optimistic delete plus a wholesale list refresh is a race: a fetch that started before the delete resolves with a pre-delete snapshot and undoes the removal. Keep short-lived tombstones, filter them out of every incoming snapshot, and retire each one when a fresh snapshot confirms the row is gone so the set stays bounded.

title: Centralise the latest-wins token so the compare is right once
statement: Stale-response guards get reimplemented per slice and get the comparison backwards, so whichever request resolves last wins even when its data is older. Extract one tiny primitive that mints a token and answers whether the caller is still the newest, and consult it in both the success and the failure branch so a stale failure cannot clear a fresh load flag.

title: Carry a monotonic key so a repeated identical arrival still fires
statement: React bails on `setState` with an unchanged value, so a deep link or request that arrives twice with the same payload silently no-ops and the user sees a stale view. Pair every 'arrival' with a monotonically increasing key so the consumer re-triggers, and bump a request token on reset so in-flight responses from a prior arrival are discarded instead of flashing into the new one.

title: Re-run one load callback on mount and after every mutation
statement: Without a data-fetching library, keep fetching predictable by giving each surface exactly one load callback that aggregates its calls and is re-run after any mutation. Accept explicitly that there is then no caching, dedupe or staleness layer anywhere — that absence is the design, and discovering it later is what hurts.

title: Give a multi-tab dashboard one fetch owner at the shell level
statement: Give a multi-tab dashboard a single pipeline hook at the shell level that owns every initial fetch, so tab switches reuse cached data and no two tabs issue the same query. Sub-tab hooks derive from the store and expose `load()` only for manual retry. Compute the effective time window once in a shared context, and split that context into a values provider and an actions provider so setter-only consumers never re-render.

title: Never preselect scopes whose export is credential-gated
statement: Preselecting credential-gated scopes turns one-click "export everything" into a blocked button. Derive passphraseRequired from the current selection, and split it from format validity so "too short" is distinguishable from "mandatory and absent".

title: Key drafts by stable identity, not render identity
statement: Draft keys are chosen for the STABLE identity, not the render identity: drafts keyed `${sourceId}::${fieldKey}` and never cleared on top-item change (a poll landing mid-typing used to wipe the half-written answer); the card id deliberately folds in sorted pending cell keys so a changed set is a genuinely different card, stable against arrival order.

title: Split live onChange from settle-only onCommit on continuous inputs
statement: Sliders and steppers should expose two callbacks with an explicit contract: `onChange` fires per tick/keystroke for live preview; `onCommit` fires once when the interaction settles (blur / Enter / pointer release) and ONLY if the value actually changed since interaction start — so expensive side effects (persistence, IPC) run once per gesture. Capture the start value in a ref and mark committed so a trailing blur after drag-release can't double-fire. Derive display precision from the step and round each clamp, or repeated +0.01 steps produce 0.30000000000000004.

title: Guard hold-to-repeat loops against buttons that become disabled mid-hold
statement: A press-and-hold repeat loop must refuse to start if the first step is already a no-op, and must end itself from inside its own tick when a step fails — because a button that becomes `disabled` mid-hold never fires pointerup/pointerleave, so the timer would outlive the gesture and spin forever.

title: Suppress the parent echo in lossy controlled round-trips with a last-emitted ref
statement: When a controlled editor's serialization is lossy (a keyless-but-valued row is dropped by rows→JSON), the parent echoing your own output back would re-derive local state from the lossy form and wipe in-progress edits. Record the exact string last emitted; when the incoming value equals it, skip re-deriving.

title: Split a form-error registry into a stable writer context and a reader context, and jump to fields without a focus fight
statement: A form-error summary needs two contexts: a stable-identity registration context every field consumes (register/unregister — never changes identity, so error churn doesn't re-render every field) and a separate errors-list context only the summary banner reads. Registration is idempotent and unregisters on unmount so conditional fields don't linger. "Jump to field" pairs smooth `scrollIntoView` with `focus({ preventScroll: true })` so the browser's instant focus-scroll doesn't fight the smooth scroll.

title: Auto-grow textareas in useLayoutEffect, resetting height to auto first
statement: Auto-growing a textarea needs both halves: reset height to `auto` before reading scrollHeight (scrollHeight never reports smaller than the current height, so the field could otherwise never shrink), and measure in `useLayoutEffect` — a passive effect makes the field visibly lag a fast typist by one character.

title: Seed a form from props only for fields the user hasn't touched
statement: When a parent passes a fresh initialValues object identity every render, a naive sync effect wipes in-progress typing. Track edited keys in a ref and only seed untouched fields from incoming props.

title: Run the full form validation gate before every side-effecting action, not just submit
statement: Test-connection, OAuth-consent and save all run the same validate() gate so a half-filled form can never start an external flow. Gate save on a passing live healthcheck only when the connector actually has one, and render the reason next to the disabled button instead of leaving a dead control.

title: Secret inputs warn on paste-error smells without blocking, with explicit paste and reveal affordances
statement: Secret capture rows warn (amber) on likely paste errors — too short, interior whitespace, unparsable URL — without hard-blocking submission; expose a paste button that trims; and wire the reveal toggle and errors with aria-pressed/aria-invalid/aria-describedby.

title: Skip wizard steps via predicates that return a user-visible reason, not by deleting them
statement: Model conditional step skipping in a guided flow as an ordered list of pure predicates, each returning a human-readable skip reason or null. Skipped steps stay in the rendered graph, labeled with why they were skipped ('Values already captured by auto-credential', 'Already authenticated via cookies (user@x)'), so the user sees the machine's reasoning instead of a mysteriously shorter plan — and adding a new skip rule is appending one predicate.

title: Modal pickers own a local draft, seeded on open, committed only on apply
statement: Every picker follows one contract: props {open, selected, onApply, onClose}; a useState draft mirroring the committed value; one if (!open) return effect that reseeds the draft, resets search/filter/step state, and schedules a cleanup-cancelled autofocus; mutation happens only in the draft until onApply. Esc-close therefore discards cleanly with zero extra code — four independent pickers share no state-management machinery.

title: Mark machine-composed section headers with an invisible sentinel so structured-freeform round-trips are lossless
statement: A structured composer serializing to 'Label: value' lines and parsing back on remount will re-bucket user text that happens to contain a colon and accumulate label prefixes on each round trip. Prefix a zero-width sentinel onto machine-emitted headers only; the parser treats a line as a section boundary only if it carries the sentinel, and unmatched lines append to the active row. Generalizes to any structured-to-freeform text bridge.

title: Buffer every wizard step as a draft and commit atomically on Finish — X must mean Cancel
statement: In a multi-step stepper modal over persisted profile state, NO step may write the store on click. All steps buffer local drafts and Finish commits them atomically; dismissal (X / Escape) discards drafts. Half-buffered designs (some steps instant-write, some buffered) silently corrupt the saved profile when a user opens the stepper to compare options and dismisses. Also re-sync each draft from the store when the store changes externally, so a stale draft can't overwrite an externally-updated value on save.

title: Pair every calibration control with a live consequence sentence computed by the same predicate the automation uses
statement: Threshold sliders and tuning levers should not end in a static caption. As the user drags, recompute the subject's status through the exact rule engine the automation will act on, and render a plain sentence stating what the system does at the current lines, right now ('X is past your red line — the system derives a goal to fix this now'). Scope the sentence to the triggers the control actually governs, and give the unmeasured case its own honest copy ('your lines take effect on the next measurement').

title: Group draft fields per save operation and assert coverage in types
statement: Model the editable entity as one flat draft type, then declare a `readonly` key array per save group (per tab / per backend operation). Derive dirty detection, baseline updates and save payloads from those arrays, and add a type-level assertion that every draft key belongs to exactly one group — so adding a field without wiring its save is a typecheck error, not a silent no-op.

title: Persist an undo before moving the baseline, or it silently vanishes
statement: In an autosaving editor, implementing undo by moving the baseline back makes the field look clean, so the autosave never reconciles storage with the undone value: the DB keeps the post-save value while the header reads 'All saved', and the undo evaporates on reload. Persist the restored state first, and only then move the baseline; on failure leave the section dirty and surface the error.

title: Guard double-submit with a ref, not with render state
statement: A `phase`/`busy` value read from the render snapshot is stale for every handler dispatched in the same tick, so two clicks (or Enter plus click) both observe the idle state and both run the mutation. The re-entry guard has to be a ref that flips synchronously before any re-render — the state flag stays, but only for rendering the disabled affordance.

title: Fold schema issues into a path-keyed error map before the UI
statement: Let one schema be the canonical shape of the entity, then flatten its validation issues into a flat map keyed by dotted field path so each control reads only its own message. Exposing the validator's raw issue array to components makes every field re-implement the search for its own error.

title: Let fields self-register errors, and split the context in two
statement: An error-summary banner for long forms shouldn't force the form owner to thread error state by hand. Have each field self-register its *visible* error with a provider, and split the context in two — one carrying register/unregister callbacks whose identity never changes (so adding an error doesn't re-render every field) and one carrying the ordered error list (so only the banner re-renders).

title: Default validation feedback to first blur, and name the policy
statement: Make *when* a field turns red a named, documented policy on the shared field wrapper — `'change' | 'blur' | 'submit'` — defaulting to `'blur'` (live only after the user has left the field once), with a `forceValidation` escape the parent form flips on submit so every error surfaces at once.

title: Debounce inline availability checks, abort stale ones, fail open
statement: Catch name collisions at type-time rather than save-time with a debounced check that passes an AbortSignal to the caller's checker, supersedes the pending timer and in-flight request on every keystroke, and — critically — falls back to idle on error so a broken check never blocks the user. Keep the surface state in `checking` between keystrokes so the spinner doesn't flicker mid-word.

title: Put the loading delay on the placeholder, never on the content
statement: Data already on screen is never hidden, dimmed, or replaced by a refetch; content renders the instant it exists. The anti-flash delay lives entirely on the skeleton — a CSS `animation-delay` of ≥120ms with `fill-mode: both`, so a fast fetch never paints a ghost — and life comes from a one-shot, id-guarded per-row cascade rather than a whole-block cross-fade.

title: Show an honest asymptotic bar for unknown-duration work
statement: A progress bar for work with only an *estimate* should run linearly to ~85% over the estimate, then crawl asymptotically toward ~98%, switch to an amber "taking longer" state past the estimate, and jump to 100% only when the work actually reports done. Never let it sit at 100% while work continues, and never let it stall at a number that looks stuck.

title: Make row entrance animations one-shot and id-guarded
statement: A stagger keyed on render index replays on every refetch, page change, and virtualized scroll — the list appears to blink continuously. Track entered row ids, mark entry on `animationend` (not mount), cap the cascade to the first viewport, expose a `resetKey` for genuine context switches, and honor prefers-reduced-motion.

title: Keep every motion timing in one preset module, as data
statement: Define every entrance/ambient/hover timing as data in a single preset module so tuning one value retunes the whole app; never inline keyframes at a call site. And know which animations your global motion config governs — an app-wide `<MotionConfig reducedMotion="always">` snaps *every* framer animation including opacity, so reveals that must survive it have to be CSS animations.

title: Animate collapse with grid rows, and keep the unmount you replaced
statement: Animating height forces a layout pass every frame; transitioning a single grid row from zero to one fraction gives the same smooth result without measuring the DOM. The migration hazard is the real lesson — the always-mounted form keeps effects, subscriptions and polling alive inside every closed section, so carry an explicit unmount option when replacing a presence-based collapse.

title: Measure adoption with a data probe, not with a 'Try it' click
statement: A feature-discovery board that marks items done because the user clicked 'Try it' measures curiosity, not adoption. Give each entry an optional `detect()` probe against real user data, promote hits to a persisted, never-unset 'done', and skip probing anything already done so the steady state costs zero IPC.

title: Float zero-setup options to the top of the first-run picker
statement: On the first-run picker, stable-partition the candidate list so options requiring no credentials/setup float to the top, keep the backend's own ordering as the tie-break within each group, and pull a larger pool than you display so the zero-setup ones can be lifted into the visible slots.

title: Cancel a tour step's queued effects, and survive a missing anchor
statement: Guided-tour / coach-mark engines schedule delayed side effects (switch a sub-tab, open a modal, set a spotlight) after navigation settles. If the user advances inside that window, the abandoned step's timeouts land on the new step. Track pending timers in a ref, clear them on step change and unmount, double-guard each callback against the current step index — and when a highlight target can't be found, flag it rather than tearing the tour down.

title: Retry a failed chunk import, but keep one stable lazy instance
statement: Wrap dynamic imports with one retry, but keep a single `React.lazy` instance. Creating a fresh lazy inside the failing promise's `.catch` races React's error propagation and re-suspends instead of throwing, so an unreachable chunk shows an infinite skeleton with no recovery.

title: Render plugin tabs from a lazy table with a self-healing allowlist
statement: A pluggable page is a static `Record<TabId, lazy(() => import())>` rendered inside exactly one ErrorBoundary and Suspense — adding a tab is a one-line diff and a failing panel cannot take the shell down. Because navigation ids usually arrive as casts from persisted or backend state, keep an explicit allowlist of what the page can actually render and reset to the default when persisted state falls outside it; otherwise a retired tab type-checks and renders blank forever.

title: Drive the router from a typed registry with a completeness guard
statement: Replace the if/else ladder that maps route → screen with a `const` map checked by `satisfies Record<RoutableSection, …>`, so adding a nav entry without a screen fails the typecheck and intentionally route-less sections must be excluded from the key type explicitly. Evaluate access gates once in the router — a gated section renders the fallback immediately instead of briefly mounting a forbidden surface before a redirect effect catches up.

title: Route mutually recursive callbacks through refs so useCallback deps stay honest
statement: When callbacks are mutually recursive (A calls B calls A), break the cycle with one ref per function: assign after definition and call via ref.current, so each useCallback keeps an honest dependency list.

title: Treat a capability-gate prop as a non-dependency; depend on the stable store action
statement: A prop that only gates capability is not a real effect dependency — depend on the stable store action instead, and document the deliberate deps deviation with the causal chain at the eslint-disable.

title: Probe localStorage once at boot, disable persistence, toast exactly once
statement: In Safari private/quota mode every setItem throws; probe once at boot, cache the verdict on globalThis (surviving HMR), keep the in-memory store functional, and toast the user exactly once.

title: Sanitize persisted enums on rehydrate through an explicit fallbacks table
statement: Migrate retired ids through an explicit fallbacks table, validate with type guards, and re-apply every DOM effect with ?? defaults for fields added later. Perf note: rAF+microtask brightness re-apply caused a post-render freeze — recalc synchronously.

title: Model a multi-scope picker as a closed union with exhaustiveness at every dispatch
statement: A multi-scope picker is a closed union with exhaustiveness forced at EVERY dispatch point (const _exhaustive: never; total Record<Kind,…>). The prior ternary chains fell through to another scope's collection, and a new kind compiled clean while mutating the wrong scope.

title: Depend a debounced auto-save on scalar fields, skip the hydration run, ref the latest
statement: In a debounced auto-save effect, depend on the setting hook's SCALAR fields, never the returned object — a fresh object per render makes the effect fire per render, the save flips a flag, and the loop never ends. Skip the first post-load run so hydration doesn't write back, and track latest prefs in a ref so rapid toggles don't lose intermediate changes.

title: Write keyed per-conversation slices and the active mirror in the same set() call
statement: For concurrent per-conversation streams with legacy flat-field consumers, a patch-builder writes the keyed slice and mirrors to the flat fields only when conversationId===active, in the SAME set() call, so there is never a torn frame; switching conversations swaps the mirror atomically and legacy setters become one-line delegates.

title: Run session side channels as stream → attach → hydrate pipelines where live wins
statement: Session-scoped side channels (recall, plan, turn summary, narration) share one pipeline: stream X → attach to episode id → hydrate from disk with LIVE entries winning (spread hydrated FIRST). Attach-time filters keep only what's worth keeping, persistence caps the newest 100, corrupt blobs degrade to no-sidecar, and the hydration dedupe mark is set BEFORE the await and UN-marked on error so transient IPC failure stays retryable.

title: Claim-and-clear one-shot store slots inside the store, acting on the returned value
statement: One-shot store slots must be read-and-cleared INSIDE the store, with callers acting on the returned value, never the closure copy — clearing the store but sending from the closure double-sent under StrictMode. Transient chat-card kinds clear at send while durable proposals hydrate PREPENDED (burying them under the current turn is how they got missed), and card patches key by durable row id after index keying wrote one card's outcome onto another post-reorder.

title: Feed a heterogeneous inbox through per-source pure adapters and a partitioning classifier
statement: A heterogeneous-source inbox uses one pure adapter per source plus a partitioning classifier that emits each row exactly once: a shared projection resolved ONCE into a Map injected into every adapter, prefixed composite ids, a first-hit-wins ladder where the explicit backend signal short-circuits an English-only heuristic scoped as approximation, and action logic held in one per-kind descriptor table.

title: Track the cursor as an ID, bound 'not now' skips, and build the numerator into the denominator
statement: A queue cursor is an ID, never an index — polls replace the queue wholesale so a remembered NUMBER means a different card; a missing id resolves to front. "Not now" is bounded (MAX_SKIP_PASSES=2) with a withoutSkip path because the bound makes accidental skips unrecoverable, and sessionTotal = resolved.size + pending.length by construction so the numerator is part of the denominator.

title: Hold a synchronous latest-known ref so rapid toggles compose instead of clobbering
statement: Any read-modify-write over a whole persisted object with async refresh needs a synchronous latest-known ref: each toggle reads and updates the ref, not the closure snapshot, so rapid toggles COMPOSE instead of clobbering each other.

title: Pair a no-replay event with a consume-on-mount latch for lazy-mounted deep links
statement: When a deep-link intent is emitted over a fire-and-forget bus toward a component that lazy-mounts, also record the intent in a single-slot module latch; the target consumes the latch on mount AND subscribes live, so the emit can never land before the subscriber exists.

title: Persist only a filter's stable dimensions; reset absolute timestamps and drill-ins on restore
statement: When persisting a view's filter state, save only the dimensions that stay meaningful across sessions (status/severity/source enums) and deliberately null out absolute timestamps and transient drill-in scopes on load, so the view never reopens into a stale or surprising deep-filter.

title: Fire the inbox-zero celebration only when a user action drained it — arm a ref, judge after settle
statement: Gate a 'you cleared it!' celebration on an armed ref set only by real user actions, evaluated after the refresh settles and only on the un-narrowed default view — so a filter change or background poll reaching zero can never trigger a false celebration.

title: When a panel re-scopes a shared store list, capture the prior query and re-issue it on unmount
statement: A surface that narrows a shared store collection to a different bucket must snapshot the query the previous consumer was using on first render and re-issue it on unmount, or the surface it borrowed the store from is left filtering the wrong bucket and renders empty after close.

title: Stamp a last-seen watermark on leaving the surface and derive 'N new since' client-side
statement: Persist an ISO last-seen timestamp when the user leaves an inbox (unmount) rather than tracking per-row read flags, then derive the 'new since your last visit' count by comparing loaded rows against the watermark — with an explicit 'mark seen' action to reset it mid-visit.

title: Model a multi-surface facet filter as one discriminated union with toggle-to-clear
statement: When several dashboard widgets (triage chips, histogram bands, momentum buckets, a table toggle) can each narrow the same list, model the active facet as a single discriminated-union value owned by the parent, with a payload-aware equality helper and a toggle helper where re-selecting the active facet clears it — every surface then renders its own pressed state and stays in sync for free.

title: An aggregate badge must sum the authoritative total plus ONLY rowless terms — and pin the arithmetic in a test
statement: Composing an "anything waiting on me?" number by hand-adding a subset of queues shows a confidently wrong 0 — worse than showing nothing. Take the backend's cross-queue total as the base, add client-side only the terms that genuinely have no backing row to count, never re-add a term the total already contains, and pin the arithmetic (including the double-count trap) in a dedicated test.

title: Clamp the current page when row count changes — never reset to page 1
statement: Resetting pagination to page 1 on every data-length change conflates a routine add/remove (deleting one row on page 4) with an actual filter change, yanking the user back to the start after ordinary edits. Keep the user's page and only pull it back when it falls out of range.

title: Version consent records, compare for equality, and badge only the newly disclosed sections on re-prompt
statement: A first-use consent stored as key-presence can never be re-asked. Store `{version}` and compare for EQUALITY (not presence) so bumping the constant re-prompts; export the literal so admin surfaces don't re-declare it; on a version bump, open and badge only the sections that are new since the accepted version, and order plain-language reassurance before admin-grade detail (a defect traced to jargon-first ordering).

title: Model multi-view flows as an FSM with a per-view transition allow-list
statement: Encode a complex navigation flow as a discriminated-union state where each state carries exactly the data it needs, validate every action against a transition table before dispatching (invalid transitions log and no-op instead of corrupting state), and derive breadcrumbs/nav-highlight purely from the state.

title: Host flow follow-ups that must outlive their trigger in a module store + app-root component
statement: When a flow's follow-up UI (post-save picker) must survive its parent unmounting on a view transition, keep its state in a module-level store, render the component once at app root, and let callers dispatch a promise-returning prompt(). Resolve any still-open previous prompt before opening a new one so callers can't deadlock.

title: Give parsed rows a synthetic stable id — never key selection on a user-supplied field
statement: Parsers legitimately emit duplicate keys (a repeated .env variable), so selection sets, React list keys and mapping alignment must use a generated id, not the parsed key — otherwise toggling one duplicate toggles them all and imports misalign.

title: Reconcile a failed optimistic delete by re-fetching, not by re-appending
statement: On rollback of an optimistic removal, prefer re-fetching the scoped list — a concurrent fetch may already have restored the item, so re-appending duplicates it. Only splice the item back (guarded by an id-presence check) when no scope key exists to re-fetch by.

title: Register middleware and listeners under a dedup key so hot-reload replaces instead of accumulates
