statement: Any module-level registry that closures register into (pipeline middleware, event handlers) must key registrations by a stable string and replace on re-registration — otherwise HMR / remount re-registers a new closure each time and handlers silently run N times. Pair the key with an explicit numeric priority plus an insertion sequence for a stable execution order.

title: Snapshot the data a post-completion hook needs into the event payload, before state resets
statement: When completion handlers reset shared state and downstream middleware still needs pre-reset facts (recent history, owner id), capture those facts into the completion payload at emit time instead of letting the middleware read the store later — by the time async middleware runs, the store has been reset or repointed at a different entity.

title: Every terminal event needs exactly one responsible finalizer — navigation must hand off, never orphan
statement: When a focused stream listener owns finalizing a run's terminal event and navigation tears that listener down mid-run, the terminal event can end up handled by NEITHER the focused nor the background listener — busy-state flags then stick until an unrelated watchdog fires. On teardown-while-running, set an explicit 'detached' flag that transfers finalization responsibility to the background listener; clear it when a fresh stream attaches.

title: Make a two-writer shared document safe with one mutable copy plus per-object author provenance
statement: When an AI agent and the user edit the same board concurrently: (1) keep ONE mutable in-memory copy that views subscribe to via useSyncExternalStore instead of snapshotting into useState — so an out-of-band write renders immediately and the next user commit builds on the post-write array, not a stale one; (2) stamp every object with an author field so the agent's objects can be visually distinguished and reverted WITHOUT touching the user's. Migration attribution must default to the human: anything not literally the agent's marker is the user's, because 'attribution can only ever ADD provenance, never take an object away from its owner'.

title: Drive a mounted view from outside by queueing typed requests it answers with honest envelopes
statement: To control a complex view (canvas, map, editor) from external callers — test harnesses, AI agents, deep links — lift the REQUEST, not the state: an external module-level queue of typed actions the view subscribes to and answers using the same callbacks its human affordances use. Every dispatch resolves (never rejects) with a result envelope carrying honest failure reasons and post-action readouts; a pickup timeout fails 'view_closed' when nothing is mounted, and callers that route first (set navigation state, then dispatch) get the timeout window as their carry-across-mount grace period.

title: Derive graph decorations in one useMemo pass instead of N setState effects
statement: When node/edge arrays are enriched by several independent concerns (base derivation, execution status, optimizer highlights, active-edge state, dry-run decorations), do NOT give each concern its own useEffect calling setNodes/setEdges — replace them with one useMemo that computes the final enriched arrays in a single pass over prebuilt O(1) lookup maps. Eliminates effect-ordering races, redundant renders, and repeated .find() scans.

title: Nesting sibling setState calls inside another updater double-applies under StrictMode
statement: React requires setState updaters to be pure. Nesting setNodeData/setCompletedEdges/setActiveEdge calls inside setStepIndex's updater means StrictMode's double-invocation applies the side-effect writes twice per step, and batching changes can reorder them. Compute the step transition OUTSIDE the updaters (read the current value, derive the next step, then issue each setState with its own pure updater).

title: A store flag that decides an overlay's mount must never also be written by the overlay
statement: When a component's mount is driven by a store flag, the component must not write that flag from its own mount/unmount effects. Under React StrictMode's mount → cleanup → mount double-invoke, the cleanup's write re-enters the parent's render mid-flush and can wedge the overlay visibly open but no longer closeable. Make the flag strictly an input; any other consumer (z-order coordination, sibling chrome) should read the same flag, not depend on the overlay echoing it.

title: Resolve a surface's landing view through a module-scoped one-shot-request > explicit-pick > size-default chain, with a pure peek and a consuming resolve
statement: When several openers promise different landing views for one surface ('this button opens the ledger'), centralize the decision in one module with three priority inputs: a one-shot request consumed on the next open (never recorded as preference), the operator's explicit pick (wins for the rest of the run), and a data-size default. Expose BOTH a side-effect-free peek (safe in render-time initializers) and a consuming resolve (called from the open effect); returning the same value from both makes the second set a no-op.

title: Prune derived id-sets against their live collection, returning the previous reference when nothing was pruned
statement: Any Set/Map of ids derived from a live collection (multi-select targets, dismissed-notification tombstones, seen-item dedupe) must be pruned whenever the collection shrinks, or it grows monotonically and acts on dead ids. The prune must return the previous reference when nothing changed — a fresh identical Set from an effect re-triggers the effect and loops the render.

title: Shared controller hook for a backend-owned recorder whose start surface can unmount before stop
statement: When a long-running recorder/job lives in the backend but its start control sits on a surface that unmounts (an overlay header), a stop control scoped to that surface strands the armed job. Route all control through one shared hook over the store: every mount adopts the backend's current status (cheap, idempotent refresh on mount, so a frontend reload rejoins an in-progress run), an always-mounted surface carries the stop control, and exactly one designated call site (poll: true) runs the status poll — and only while the job is active, so an idle system does no background work.

title: Serialize read-modify-write of a shared persisted blob through one module write queue
statement: When multiple components can concurrently read-modify-write the same persisted JSON blob or conversation log, funnel every mutation through a module-scoped promise chain so each mutation reads the LATEST state after previous writes have landed. Without it the last writer silently wins and drops sibling updates. Return a typed {applied, reason} result so callers can distinguish no-op from conflict.

title: Stamp cached async results with their owning entity and guard both write and read
statement: A result map keyed only by item id bleeds across entity switches: a tool run started under persona A lands keyed by toolId and surfaces under persona B. Stamp each entry with the owning entity captured at call time, drop the write if the current entity ref changed during flight, and as defense-in-depth hide mismatched entries at read time. Update the current-entity ref synchronously in the render body — a useEffect-updated ref is one render stale for microtask-resolved results.

title: Keep live handles in module maps beside the store; the store holds only serializable runtime
statement: When a Zustand store owns long-running per-entity runtime (so work continues while the user navigates elsewhere), keep non-serializable handles — poll timers, auto-advance timers, event unlisten functions — in module-scoped Maps keyed by entity id NEXT TO the store, never inside store state. The store stays a serializable snapshot (persistable, devtools-safe); the maps carry the machinery.

title: Per-variant UI branches copy-pasted instead of table-driven, plus identity-based state matching
statement: Two ~36-line blocks differing only in a channel string and two i18n keys sit in a file that already proves the table-driven alternative works; worse, both match the array element to update by object identity (if (s !== spec) return s), which silently no-ops if any upstream code maps or clones the draft array — the same file's other updater correctly matches by stable key fields. Review checklist for any picker that has grown per-variant special cases.

title: Reset every piece of component-local UI state when the session/entity identity changes — standardize a resetKey prop
statement: Store-mirrored data resets itself when a new session starts, but component-local pickers, modal flags, and prefills do not — the observed bug was a blank questionnaire window from a stale index carried across drafts. Every stateful surface gets one effect keyed on the entity id that nulls its whole local block, generalized in hooks as a resetKey prop rather than relying on key= remounts alone.

title: Read the previous session's watermark in a render-time initializer — child effects advance it before parent effects run
statement: When a surface both consumes a persisted last-seen watermark and advances it on a heartbeat, freeze the previous-session value in a `useState` lazy initializer during the FIRST render. React runs child effects before parent effects, so a parent that reads the watermark in its own effect gets the value a child heartbeat already overwrote. Pair this with a module-scoped once-per-session latch (surviving remounts, reset on reload) plus an exported test-only reset.

title: The storage event never fires in the writing window — pair persisted markers with an in-process subscriber list
statement: In a single-window shell (Tauri/Electron), relying on the `storage` event to observe a localStorage marker is dead code: the event fires only in OTHER windows/tabs, never in the writer. Keep the marker in localStorage for reload survival, but layer a tiny module-level subscriber Set on top so live components re-read on every write — and document which signals are the ONLY re-read triggers, so nobody re-adds a proxy dependency (like array length) that misses same-entity repeat writes.

title: A delayed navigation side effect must re-validate the route it assumed before landing
statement: Deep links and guided flows that set a section first and its sub-tab on a short timeout (so the section can mount) must re-check, inside the timeout callback, that the user is still where the scheduler assumed — still on the routed section, still on the scheduling step. Otherwise a stale timer yanks the user to a tab of a screen they already left. Use defense in depth: clear pending timeouts on state change AND re-check inside each callback, so a missed clear still can't misfire.

title: Read a heavy store from a light surface via lazy import plus manual subscribe
statement: When a lightweight always-mounted surface needs a small slice of a heavy feature store, dynamically import the store inside an effect: seed local state from whatever the store already cached, trigger the store's fetch only when the cache is empty, and stay subscribed with an identity-compare so updates flow live. This keeps the heavy store off the surface's eager bundle and — by making the store the single source — collapses duplicate data paths (the old code ran a parallel 30s IPC poll for the same rows).

title: Migrate flow progress across tier variants through shared step ids
statement: When the same guided flow ships in two tier variants (full vs simple), give the overlapping steps identical ids in both registries and, on tier switch, mark any step completed in one variant as completed in the other. Migration is one-directional per activation (into the newly-started variant) and leaves the other variant's persisted progress untouched, so a tier flip-flop loses no work in either direction.

title: After promoting a new default, enumerate the per-item overrides that now diverge and offer clear-or-keep — keep is a first-class no-op
statement: Promoting a new default (model, template, policy) leaves per-item override pins untouched, so items silently keep executing on the old value. Immediately after a successful promotion, surface a reconciliation dialog listing exactly which items still pin something else, let the user clear each pin (write through the same shared mutator as every other edit — no parallel write path) or keep it, and skip reconciliation entirely when the promotion write itself failed.

title: Hydrate from local storage first, then reconcile with the server
statement: Cross-cutting state that must work offline and signed-out belongs in one context that hydrates locally on mount and then reconciles against the server copy for authenticated users, with a documented winner and a one-time backfill. Treat a failed server call as non-fatal and keep the local copy; prop-drilling the same state instead scatters the reconciliation policy across every consumer.

title: Persist a background session's view state and re-attach on reload
statement: When the real work lives in a server/native process that outlives the UI, the in-memory view state is the fragile half. Persist the open-tab set plus a bounded log of what happened, then on mount probe each session's health and re-attach when it is alive — cold-starting only when it genuinely isn't. Otherwise a webview reload shows an empty screen while the process keeps running.

title: Namespace persisted view preferences by view id, and guard the parse
statement: Sort order, column widths, scroll offset and collapse state are user work — persist them, but namespace the storage key by a caller-supplied view id so each table remembers its own layout, wrap every read/write in try/catch that logs rather than throws, and only commit a persisted change when the interaction was deliberate.

title: Rehydrate derived state from a remount cache, not just the input
statement: Caching UI input in a module-level variable so it survives a remount only restores half the world: the control shows the old value while the list it filters is unfiltered. Rehydrate once on mount behind a ref guard, pushing the cached value back through the same callbacks a real edit would fire.

title: Own durable state on the server; keep client state ephemeral
statement: When the server can be the single owner of durable state, client components need no global store at all — tenant-scoped server-side stores hold everything durable and components keep only ephemeral UI state. The alternative mirrors server data into a client store and then spends its life reconciling two sources of truth.

title: Refetch after each mutation instead of keeping a client cache
statement: With the database as the sole source of truth, each panel can hold local state and re-fetch its own endpoint after every mutation — no client cache means no stale-cache bugs. The cost is that every panel re-implements the loading/error/refetch triangle by hand, so this only holds while the panel count stays small.

title: Share one small client-only value with a module-level pub/sub
statement: A single small value shared by a handful of components does not justify a state library: module-level functions over local storage plus a listener set and a subscribing hook give cross-component and cross-tab sync in a few dozen lines. The failure this replaces is not a missing library but the same logic inlined per file.

title: Split global state into many small stores, not one combined object
statement: Independently-imported stores per concern keep subscriptions narrow and tree-shaking effective, while a combined root store is a convenience that quietly re-renders unrelated surfaces. Where a combined accessor exists, document it as the exception, and keep superseded flat stores as re-export shims so the migration path stays visible instead of looking like drift.

title: Absorb history at mount and bound every set a live overlay grows
statement: A pop-up layer that diffs a snapshot feed has four failure modes that only appear in long sessions: a startup blast of historical items, an unbounded seen-set, an unbounded tombstone-set, and an auto-dismiss timer that restarts on every re-render. Fix all four explicitly — the first three with a mount grace window and periodic pruning, the last by keying the timer on the item id and holding the callback in a ref.

title: Make the unmount guard automatic in the hook, never opt-in
statement: If safety requires the call site to invoke a returned `cleanup()`, most call sites won't — the protection silently never runs. Make the guard automatic inside the hook, and make it re-arm on mount so StrictMode's double-invoke doesn't leave it disarmed.

title: Tear down subscriptions on re-entry, and store the listen promise
statement: Two subscription leaks recur with async `listen()` APIs. Re-entering a start path overwrites the stored unlisten set, orphaning the previous subscriptions forever with nothing able to reach them — so tear down before subscribing again, and filter every handler by the job id it belongs to. And an unmount that fires before `listen()` resolves has no unlisten function to call: store the PROMISE and tear down with `.then((fn) => fn())`.

title: Give every orphan class its own bucket in a hierarchical view
statement: A tree or matrix assembled from a join will always have rows whose parent is missing, null, or was removed by a rescan. Enumerate those classes explicitly and give each a synthetic parent node — group-level, project-level, ungrouped, unassigned — rather than filtering them out. A row that vanishes from a management surface is indistinguishable from a row that does not exist.

title: Resolve entity state once, then fold it per view density
statement: A monitoring surface usually ships several densities (large cards, compact rows, a grid of squares). Resolve the entity's state ONCE in a priority-ordered function, then have each density fold that key into fewer buckets. Every view then agrees about colour and urgency by construction.

title: Derive view rows in a React-free, store-free model module
statement: Put the mapping from storage shape to decided view row — defaults applied, names resolved, groups computed, comparators defined — in a pure module with no JSX, no i18n and no store access. Every surface then consumes the same decided shape and the same comparator, so a table, a card deck and a badge can never disagree; and the derivation is trivially unit-testable.
